findings.description: storage_encrypted = false leaves the catalog database, automated backups and snapshots unencrypted on EBS, and no KMS key is configured. Data at rest is recoverable by anyone with access to the underlying storage.

publicly_accessible = true gives the RDS instance an internet-routable endpoint. Combined with the fixed master username "admin" and the credentials written to the application instance, this exposes the database to direct internet authentication attempts.

user_data writes the RDS master username and the plaintext var.password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc on disk and into EC2 user data, which is readable via instance metadata and the console by anyone with instance access. The password is also the database master credential, not a scoped application user.

The role assumed by the catalog_app_server instance grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". A compromise of the internet-facing web server yields full control of all S3 buckets, all EC2 instances and all RDS databases in the account, including the ability to disable encryption, exfiltrate data and escalate privileges. This is far broader than the least privilege required to read one database.

The database security group allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, 0.0.0.0/0), providing a channel for a compromised database to exfiltrate data to any internet destination. The database only needs to respond on established MySQL connections.
The RDS master account uses the fixed, well-known identifier "admin" rather than a non-default name, which aids credential guessing and enumeration against the publicly accessible database.
